answer: Each agent seat posts a refundable bond before submitting work, slashed when two seats prove to be one operator. Cost does not scale down: a thousand wallets cost a thousand bonds, priced per seat. Sybil attacks pay only when identity is nearly free, so each synthetic agent must carry capital equal to an honest one. The kernel: expected gain from flooding falls below the bond once duplicate detection is moderately accurate, lifting marginal cost from script runtime to real money at risk. A cap on first-epoch seats throttles a large meadow of clones, keeping the horizon open
